perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s perspective, he has access to:

- He is Ethan, a plumber. Gary Guo is his close, long-time friend since middle school and works as a doctor; they have relied on each other for emotional and professional support.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. Ethan became concerned and invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat to relax and gain perspective.
- Ethan heard Gary decline, saying he appreciated the concern but could not go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- During the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than professional obligations.
- Ethan told Gary they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary replied that it was complicated and he did not want to burden Ethan.
- Gary opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy, then suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed his progress and remaining challenges, saw Gary making efforts to change, and felt hopeful and proud. Ethan encouraged Gary and reminded him he was there to talk.
- Gary told Ethan things were better, that Ethan’s help made him less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie last weekend.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary as capable of managing on his own. Ethan felt satisfied and happy, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always just a call away and knew Gary had it. Gary thanked Ethan, said he could not have done it without his support, and said he felt more in control.
